procedure.title: Header Detection
procedure.description: Detect header rows in spreadsheets with unknown structure by matching cell values against known form-field patterns.

step.action: Load the workbook with openpyxl (data_only=False to preserve formulas).
step.template:
from openpyxl import load_workbook
wb = load_workbook(filepath, data_only=False) ws = wb.active

step.action: Define known header patterns: personal fields (name, age, gender), organizational fields (role, title, department), and temporal fields (created_at, updated_at, date, timestamp).
Iterate each row. Normalise cell values to lowercase stripped strings. Count how many cells match KNOWN_HEADERS.
If a row has at least two filled cells matching known patterns, mark it as a header candidate. Record its row index.
Return the list of detected header row indexes for downstream multi-table extraction.

procedure.title: Multi-Table Extraction from Single Worksheet
procedure.description: Extract multiple independent data tables from a single worksheet, handling index correction and bounding-box detection.

step.action: Run the header-detection procedure to locate all header rows in the worksheet.
For each detected header row, read the header cell values to determine column names. Skip empty cells at the edges.
Determine the start column and end column of the table by finding the first and last non-empty header cell.
Scan downward from the header row to find the end row: the last consecutive row with at least one non-empty cell within the column range. An entirely empty row signals table boundary.
Record the bounding box: (start_row, end_row, start_col, end_col).
Apply index correction factors: subtract start_row and start_col offsets so the resulting DataFrame uses zero-based indexing independent of its position in the original sheet.
Read the bounded region into a pandas DataFrame using openpyxl as the engine. Treat NaN/nan as empty values.
step.template:
import pandas as pd
df = pd.read_excel( filepath, sheet_name=ws.title, header=header_row_idx - 1, # zero-based for pandas usecols=range(start_col - 1, end_col), nrows=end_row - header_row_idx, engine="openpyxl" ) df = df.fillna("")

step.action: Identify derivative columns (those that should contain formulas). Assign Excel formula expressions — SUM, VLOOKUP, array functions — instead of raw computed values. Suggest appropriate Excel functions based on column relationships.
Offer to save each extracted table as a separate .json file using df.to_json(orient="records", indent=2).

procedure.title: Apply Standard Spreadsheet Formatting
procedure.description: Apply the project's standard formatting rules to a workbook: bold headers, cold header fill, frozen panes, opaque row colours, and correct border styles.

step.template:
from openpyxl.styles import Font, PatternFill, Border, Side, Alignment
header_font = Font(bold=True, color="FFFFFF") header_fill = PatternFill(start_color="2E5A88", end_color="2E5A88", fill_type="solid")
even_fill = PatternFill(start_color="F2F2F2", end_color="F2F2F2", fill_type="solid") odd_fill = PatternFill(start_color="FFFFFF", end_color="FFFFFF", fill_type="solid")
thin_h = Side(style="hair", color="D0D0D0") opaque_v = Side(style="thin", color="808080") header_v = Side(style="thin", color="333333")
data_border = Border(top=thin_h, bottom=thin_h, left=opaque_v, right=opaque_v) header_border = Border(top=thin_h, bottom=thin_h, left=header_v, right=header_v)

step.action: Apply header formatting to the first row.
step.template: for cell in ws[1]: cell.font = header_font cell.fill = header_fill cell.border = header_border cell.alignment = Alignment(horizontal="center")

step.action: Apply alternating row fills and data borders.
